page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9ae.large is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by KVM virtualization. The instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs based on AMD EPYC 9T95 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a base clock speed of 2.25 GHz. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM allocated per core.

Storage and networking configurations reflect a modular cloud design. The ecs.c9ae.large does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence and operational file systems. Networking performance provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and the configuration does not provision complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Designed for entry-level computational duties, the 1:2 resource allocation offers cost efficiency for applications where processor cycles take precedence over memory capacity. Tradeoffs include limited total memory headroom and the absence of high-speed local NVMe disks, which restricts suitability for heavy memory-caching layers or I/O-intensive database engines. Appropriate workloads include front-end web serving, application microservices, batch processing, proxy nodes, and lightweight continuous integration workers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9ae.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by 2 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor running at 2.25 GHz on x86_64 architecture, it is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates without integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached volumes for data retention. Network throughput features a baseline capacity of 2 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. By focusing resources on dedicated CPU capacity rather than substantial memory overhead, ecs.c9ae.large delivers a cost-efficient footprint for compute-oriented tasks with moderate memory requirements. The instance is suited for containerized microservices, light batch data transformation, load balancing, API routing, and distributed front-end web serving architectures.
